title: "Area 51 has been suspect for years": Secretary of Energy addresses alleged UFO sightings at nuclear sites
excerpt: In a recent podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, former Secretary of Energy John S. Herrington discussed alleged UFO sightings at nuclear sites.
content:
Archi Biswas

Updated Thu, October 8, 2026 at 9:26 AM UTC

In a recent podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, former Secretary of Energy John S. Herrington discussed alleged UFO sightings at nuclear sites. Herrington served as the Secretary of Energy from 1985 to 1989 under President Ronald Reagan. When Michels asked the former Secretary of Energy about UFO sightings in nuclear sites, mostly Air Force bases and national labs, like F.E. Warren AFB, Ellsworth AFB, and Malmstrom AFB, Seal Beach, and the like, he said,

"I don't have any information to give you. I will tell you Area 51 has been suspect for years. There's a lot going on there on defense related activities, but nothing that I know about with any kind of UFOs."

John S. Herrington on UFO files, Area 51, AI, and more

During the podcast, John S. Herrington clarified that Area 51 has been a suspect for UFO sightings for years. However, he had never encountered evidence of UFOs or non-human technology during his tenure overseeing the nuclear complex. He acknowledged that the recent UAP videos released by the Navy were not fake.

Later in the interview, Michels spoke about Reagan's statement regarding UFOs. Michels explained that in 1974, while Reagan was governor in California, he and a pilot named Bill Painter were flying together in a Cessna near Bakersfield. According to Michels, Painter said that they saw a UFO 100 yards behind the plane, and it suddenly accelerated, elongated, and shot 45 degrees upwards. According to the host, Reagan jokingly instructed Painter to follow it.

Herrington claimed that he heard about the incident and went on to narrate an incident when Painter dropped him off at the wrong destination.

Speaking about AI and its impact, Herrington claimed that it is difficult to trust what's real and what's not. He said that he would now be a skeptic.

Michels also spoke about Marco Rubio, the Secretary of State and National Security Advisor, who said that things are flying over military installations and advised that they should look into it.

Herrington responded, saying,

"I would believe that. I would go along with that, but I can't go to the next step. What is it? I have no idea."

When asked about the extraterrestrial sightings, he said that he had seen pictures on television and films about UFOs and called them rumors.

John S. Herrington on UFOs and Navy Videos

When Michels asked Herrington whether he experienced anything related to the UAP sightings while he was Secretary of Energy, Herrington responded, saying that they got a lot of rumors about activities in Area 51. He described Area 51 as a highly classified space with multiple classified projects, primarily related to defense, being carried out. He continued,

"Nothing about UFOs and honestly I did not during the time I was there come across anything in our budgets or in our programs that would lead me to have any knowledge in the UFO area."

However, he acknowledged seeing reports on television about mysterious objects captured by the Navy's gun cameras near San Diego. He recalled seeing the footage of the mysterious thing traveling at warp speed before diving straight into the ocean. Herrington said that he does not know what these objects are or where they came from. However, he added, in his opinion, the recent UAP videos were not fake. He maintained that he never encountered evidence of aliens during his tenure but expressed curiosity about the phenomena.
